title: Can You Cut an Atom? Dalton Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Crush a sugar crystal finer and finer: can you go on forever? Why does well water and rain water have the same recipe, and where does a candle's wax go? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) one idea from 1808 answers all three: John Dalton's atomic theory.

You will watch a grain of matter cut into 2, 4, 8 and 16 pieces until it reaches an atom, then put Dalton's four postulates on the molecule bench: indivisible atoms, identical atoms of one element (about 16 hydrogen atoms balance one oxygen atom), atoms joining in a fixed ratio (H2O, two hydrogens to one oxygen, held by shared electron pairs), and reactions that only rearrange atoms (2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, atoms counted on both sides). We compare water with hydrogen peroxide, then link Dalton's ideas to the laws of conservation of mass, definite proportions and multiple proportions (16 g : 32 g of oxygen = 1 : 2). A worked example splits 72 g of water into 8 g hydrogen and 64 g oxygen. Then what survived and what broke (atoms have parts, isotopes like chlorine-35 and chlorine-37, the law of gaseous volumes), the isotope exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 7 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
